title: exosat-rv: a Python workflow for radial-velocity exosatellite searches around directly imaged companions
description: A Python toolkit and research workflow for companion-side radial-velocity searches using public ESO archive data. It inventories CRIRES+ holdings, converts ESO ADP spectra into the cr2res layout consumed by viper, tests alias structure and model comparisons, and provides feasibility calculations; accompanying scripts drive the from-raw cr2res/viper analysis. In a separately implemented extraction calibrated against the published CD-35 2722 B RV series, a downstream search recovers the reported approximately 171-day signal on the 17 nights retained by an internal quality screen, while the all-18-night series degrades to noise. Its model fits do not ingest the published RV values, but the historical driver constructs a paper-matched subset and hard-codes a 171.45-day reporting window; the search is target- and paper-aware. The result is therefore conditional on the screen and is not an end-to-end independent reproduction. Signal injection shifts an already-built template and validates fitter-stage transmission, not possible absorption during template construction. The apparent transfer to staring mode was withdrawn after those data were identified as HiRISE fibre observations reduced with a slit recipe. The adopted M14/M15 RV, per-order/BERV, parameter, and target artifacts are frozen in data/repro with the VIPER configuration and tracked source patch observed in the audited checkout, plus a hash manifest. That configuration records checkout state only; it does not prove which configuration governed the historical extraction runs. Raw/reduced ESO spectra and fitted templates remain external; the templates are hash-bound, so Git alone does not replay raw exposures through template construction. No discovery is claimed and nothing has been submitted.
